socfpga_i3c_ll.h

I3C low-level driver interface for the SoCFPGA bare-metal software stack.

Constants
SOCFPGA_I3C_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT

The standard active-polling limit for low-level synchronous FIFO and Queue operations before yielding a hardware timeout fault.

socfpga_i3c_ll_enable
int32_t socfpga_i3c_ll_enable(
uint32_t 
base_address,
bool 
enable
)

Directly manipulates the Device Control Register to assert or deassert the primary enable bit of the I3C Master controller.

Parameters
base_address
uint32_t

The physical MMIO base address of the target I3C instance.

enable
bool

true to enable the core logic and bus drivers; false to disable.

Returns

0 on success; -EINVAL if the base address is invalid.

socfpga_i3c_ll_soft_reset
int32_t socfpga_i3c_ll_soft_reset(
uint32_t 
base_address,
uint32_t 
reset_mask
)

Triggers a localized soft reset of the I3C Master controller via the hardware Reset Control Register. This flushes the TX/RX FIFOs, clears the Command and Response queues, and resets internal state machines without requiring a full system-level peripheral reset.

Parameters
base_address
uint32_t

The physical MMIO base address of the target I3C instance.

reset_mask
uint32_t

A hardware-specific bitmask dictating which sub-blocks to reset (e.g., FIFOs only vs. entire controller).

Returns

0 on success.

socfpga_i3c_ll_enable_interrupts
int32_t socfpga_i3c_ll_enable_interrupts(
uint32_t 
base_address,
uint32_t 
mask,
bool 
signal
)

Modifies the Interrupt Mask Register to selectively route internal hardware events (such as RX Buffer Full, TX Buffer Empty, or Response Queue Ready) to the system's Generic Interrupt Controller (GIC).

Parameters
base_address
uint32_t

The physical MMIO base address of the target I3C instance.

mask
uint32_t

The specific interrupt status bits to modify.

signal
bool

true to unmask (enable) the interrupt generation; false to mask (disable).

Returns

0 on success.

socfpga_i3c_ll_send_command
int32_t socfpga_i3c_ll_send_command(
uint32_t 
base_address,
uint32_t 
command,
const 
uint32_t 
*
data_words,
uint32_t 
word_count,
uint32_t 
timeout
)

Orchestrates a low-level enqueue operation. This function writes a fully formatted 32-bit instruction into the hardware Command Queue (CQ), and subsequently pushes the associated payload into the Transmit (TX) FIFO.

Parameters
base_address
uint32_t

The physical MMIO base address of the target I3C instance.

command
uint32_t

The 32-bit encoded I3C command descriptor.

data_words
const uint32_t*

Pointer to the payload buffer.

word_count
uint32_t

Number of 32-bit words to push to the TX FIFO.

timeout
uint32_t

Maximum polling iterations to wait for FIFO space before aborting.

Returns

0 on success; -ETIMEDOUT if the hardware FIFOs remain full and cannot accept data.

socfpga_i3c_ll_read_response
int32_t socfpga_i3c_ll_read_response(
uint32_t 
base_address,
uint32_t 
*
response,
uint32_t 
timeout
)

Actively polls the Response Queue (RQ) for a transaction completion descriptor.  This 32-bit word contains the final status of a bus transfer, including data lengths and error flags (e.g., NACK, Parity Error).

Parameters
base_address
uint32_t

The physical MMIO base address of the target I3C instance.

response
uint32_t*

Pointer to a 32-bit variable where the response descriptor will be written.

timeout
uint32_t

Maximum polling iterations to wait for the RQ to flag ready.

Returns

0 on success; -ETIMEDOUT if the controller fails to produce a response.

socfpga_i3c_ll_read_data
int32_t socfpga_i3c_ll_read_data(
uint32_t 
base_address,
uint32_t 
*
data_words,
uint32_t 
word_count,
uint32_t 
timeout
)

Drains incoming 32-bit words from the hardware Receive (RX) FIFO. The driver monitors the RX Buffer Level register to ensure it only reads valid data shifted in from the I3C bus.

Parameters
base_address
uint32_t

The physical MMIO base address of the target I3C instance.

data_words
uint32_t*

Pointer to the destination buffer.

word_count
uint32_t

The number of 32-bit words to extract from the FIFO.

timeout
uint32_t

Maximum polling iterations to wait for data to become available.

Returns

0 on success; -ETIMEDOUT if the expected data does not arrive.

socfpga_i3c_ll_program_dat_entry
int32_t socfpga_i3c_ll_program_dat_entry(
uint32_t 
base_address,
uint32_t 
device_index,
uint8_t 
address,
bool 
legacy_i2c
)

Configures a specific slot within the controller's Device Address Table (DAT).  The hardware uses this table to resolve the `device_index` supplied in Command Queue descriptors to actual 7-bit bus addresses and protocol rules.

Parameters
base_address
uint32_t

The physical MMIO base address of the target I3C instance.

device_index
uint32_t

The hardware DAT slot to program (typically 0-15).

address
uint8_t

The 7-bit static I2C or dynamically assigned I3C device address.

legacy_i2c
bool

true if the device lacks I3C support, forcing the hardware to use standard I2C timing and protocols for this index.

Returns

0 on success; -EINVAL if the device index exceeds hardware limits.

socfpga_i3c_ll_private_transfer
int32_t socfpga_i3c_ll_private_transfer(
uint32_t 
base_address,
uint32_t 
device_index,
bool 
read,
const 
uint8_t 
*
tx_buffer,
uint32_t 
tx_length,
uint8_t 
*
rx_buffer,
uint32_t 
rx_length,
uint32_t 
timeout,
uint32_t 
*
response
)

A monolithic helper function to execute a complete, synchronous read or write transaction. It formats the Command Queue descriptor, manages the TX/RX FIFOs, and waits for the Response Queue to confirm completion, returning the result to the caller.

Parameters
base_address
uint32_t

The physical MMIO base address of the target I3C instance.

device_index
uint32_t

The DAT index identifying the target peripheral.

read
bool

true for a read transaction; false for a write transaction.

tx_buffer
const uint8_t*

Pointer to the data to send (ignored if `read` is true).

tx_length
uint32_t

Number of bytes to send.

rx_buffer
uint8_t*

Pointer to the buffer for receiving data (ignored if `read` is false).

rx_length
uint32_t

Number of bytes to receive.

timeout
uint32_t

Maximum polling iterations for the entire transaction.

response
uint32_t*

Pointer to store the final Response Queue hardware descriptor.

Returns

0 on success; -EIO or -ETIMEDOUT on a bus failure.

socfpga_i3c_ll_get_status
uint32_t socfpga_i3c_ll_get_status(
uint32_t 
base_address
)

Reads the raw, unmasked Interrupt Status Register. This reveals the immediate physical state of the controller, indicating events such as Bus Errors, Hot-Join Requests, or FIFO thresholds.

Parameters
base_address
uint32_t

The physical MMIO base address of the target I3C instance.

Returns

The raw 32-bit hardware status value.

socfpga_i3c_ll_get_hw_capability
uint32_t socfpga_i3c_ll_get_hw_capability(
uint32_t 
base_address
)

Extracts the read-only synthesis parameters from the Hardware Capability register. This provides the driver with immutable IP block properties, such as the maximum supported DAT entries, FIFO depths, and HDR mode support.

Parameters
base_address
uint32_t

The physical MMIO base address of the target I3C instance.

Returns

The 32-bit hardware capability identifier block.

socfpga_i3c_ll_read_reg
uint32_t socfpga_i3c_ll_read_reg(
uint32_t 
base_address,
uint32_t 
offset
)

Performs a direct 32-bit Memory-Mapped I/O (MMIO) read from an arbitrary register offset within the I3C instance.

Parameters
base_address
uint32_t

The physical MMIO base address of the target I3C instance.

offset
uint32_t

The exact 32-bit aligned register offset.

Returns

The raw 32-bit hardware value.

Notes

This is an intentionally thin, lockless helper. It expects the caller to validate the address and offset.

socfpga_i3c_ll_write_reg
void socfpga_i3c_ll_write_reg(
uint32_t 
base_address,
uint32_t 
offset,
uint32_t 
value
)

Performs a direct 32-bit Memory-Mapped I/O (MMIO) write to an arbitrary register offset within the I3C instance.

Parameters
base_address
uint32_t

The physical MMIO base address of the target I3C instance.

offset
uint32_t

The exact 32-bit aligned register offset.

value
uint32_t

The 32-bit data payload to commit.

Returns

None.

Notes

This is an intentionally thin, lockless helper. It expects the caller to validate the address and handle any required memory synchronization barriers.
